intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma syndrome-8 (PPGL8) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the TMEM127 gene (613403) on chromosome 2q11.2.

paragraphs.text: Pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma syndrome-8 (PPGL8) is an autosomal dominant tumor predisposition caused by germline TMEM127 mutations. It mainly causes pheochromocytoma, which may be bilateral or multicentric and usually appears in adulthood. Paraganglioma and renal cell carcinoma are seen less often, and metastatic disease is rare (Yao et al., 2010; Toledo et al., 2015; Armaiz-Pena et al., 2021).

checks.claim: PPGL8 is an autosomal dominant tumor predisposition caused by germline TMEM127 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: We recently identified germline mutations of the novel transmembrane-encoding gene FP/TMEM127 in familial and sporadic pheochromocytomas consistent with a tumor suppressor effect.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports germline mutations and familial cases. It does not explicitly state autosomal dominant inheritance.

checks.claim: PPGL8 mainly causes pheochromocytoma.
checks.evidence_quote: Germline mutations of FP/TMEM127 were associated with pheochromocytoma but not paraganglioma
checks.explanation: The paper states the mutations are associated with pheochromocytoma, and all carriers had adrenal tumors.

checks.claim: Pheochromocytoma in PPGL8 may be bilateral or multicentric.
checks.evidence_quote: Tumors were multicentric in five (45%) and bilateral in five (45%) patients.

checks.claim: Pheochromocytoma in PPGL8 usually appears in adulthood.
checks.evidence_quote: The median age at disease onset in the FP/TMEM127 mutation group was similar to that of patients without a mutation (41.5 vs 45 years, respectively; P = .54).
checks.explanation: A median onset age of 41.5 years supports onset in adulthood.

paragraphs.text: Toledo et al. (2015) studied a 6-generation family in which 47 of 151 relatives carried a TMEM127 mutation. Clinical data were available for 34 mutation carriers, who were followed for 8.7 +/- 8.1 years (range, 1-20 years). Pheochromocytoma was diagnosed in 11 carriers (32%) at a median age of 43 years. Tumors were multicentric in 5 patients (45%) and bilateral in 5 (45%). Six patients (54%) had at least 1 adrenomedullary nodule smaller than 10 mm. No paragangliomas, distant metastases, or other manifestations were detected. In 9 patients, symptoms began at 29 years (range, 10-55 years); 2 patients were asymptomatic. The youngest patient was diagnosed at age 22 years, and the earliest symptoms were reported at age 10. Cumulative penetrance of pheochromocytoma was 0% at 0 to 20 years, 3% at 21 to 30 years, 15% at 31 to 40 years, 24% at 41 to 50 years, and 32% at 51 to 65 years. The authors concluded that multicentric tumors, nodular adrenomedullary hyperplasia, and symptoms beginning more than a decade before diagnosis were novel findings in TMEM127-related pheochromocytoma.

During the same period she had paroxysmal hypertensive crises, with systolic blood pressure up to 240 mmHg, accompanied by headache, flushing, and chest tightness. She had a neck paraganglioma and acromegaly due to a growth hormone-secreting pituitary macroadenoma, with elevated IGF1, macroglossia, and snoring. She also had a multinodular goiter and colonic polyps. Plasma free metanephrines were normal. She carried a heterozygous TMEM127 variant of uncertain significance.

paragraphs.text: Armaiz-Pena et al. (2021) described 110 index patients with germline TMEM127 variants. The mean age was 45 years (range, 21-84 years), and females predominated (76 vs 34; P less than 0.001). Most patients had pheochromocytoma (94; 85.5%). Paraganglioma (10; 9%) and renal cell carcinoma (6; 5.4%) were also found, either alone or together with pheochromocytoma. One-third of patients had multiple tumors, and 15.4% reported a known family history. Metastatic pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma was rare (2.8%). In 82% of tumors, the catecholamine profile was epinephrine alone or with norepinephrine. The authors concluded that patients with TMEM127 variants often resemble patients with sporadic nonmetastatic pheochromocytoma. They noted that paraganglioma and renal cell carcinoma may co-occur but that the causal link needed further evaluation.

paragraphs.text: Yao et al. (2010) sequenced the FP/TMEM127 gene in 990 individuals with pheochromocytoma and/or paraganglioma. These included 898 previously unreported cases without mutations in other susceptibility genes. The authors found 19 potentially pathogenic germline heterozygous mutations in 20 independent families. Multiplex PCR screening of 545 samples detected no large deletions. Confocal microscopy of 5 novel mutant proteins expressed in cell lines showed diffuse localization, whereas wild-type TMEM127 had a discrete multiorganelle distribution.

paragraphs.text: Takeichi et al. (2012) sequenced TMEM127 in 74 unrelated Japanese patients with pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma who tested negative for RET, VHL, SDHB, and SDHD mutations. Two patients (2.7%) with bilateral adrenal pheochromocytoma carried the same heterozygous germline 4-bp deletion (c.116_119delTGTC; p.Ile41ArgfsTer39). None of 114 ethnically matched healthy controls carried the deletion. The authors noted that the same mutation had been reported previously in a Brazilian case.
